target.statement: VEN-VL with a Qwen3-0.6B LLM backbone retains 7.5% of visual tokens and reaches 50.3 on AI2D, outperforming token-pruning baselines under identical training data (stop-pruning comparison).
target.table_ref: Table 2 (VEN-VL row, AI2D column), ablated in Table 3
target.dataset: LLaVA-1.5 instruction data (alignment: LCS-558K; SFT: ~10M mixed instruction data), evaluated on AI2D

compute.basis: Every headline/number in Tables 1-3 comes from a freshly trained VLM (frozen-encoder alignment stage on 558K pairs plus full SFT on a ~10M-sample instruction mix with MoE experts, dual encoders and SIP loss); even the smallest backbone (Qwen3-0.6B) needs a multi-day GPU training run, which is orders of magnitude beyond an 8-core CPU-only laptop.

blockers: No trained checkpoints or reproducible configs are guaranteed by the single GitHub link; results in the paper come from training, not inference of a released model
Requires two-stage VLM training (alignment + SFT) on ~10M instruction samples with MoE visual experts, SIP loss and custom merge operators
Two visual encoders (CLIP-ViT-L/14-336 and RADIOv2.5) plus variable-resolution tiling; heavy preprocessing/feature extraction
The only seemingly training-free result (applying HTE to Kimi-VL-16B-A3B, Table 7) requires inference of a 16B MoE model over full MME/MMB/GQA/AI2D/TextVQA benchmarks, far beyond 16 GB RAM / CPU
No GPU available in the target environment; training would be infeasible on CPU
title: VEN-VL: A Visual Ensemble MoE Framework for Effective and Efficient Multi-Modal Understanding
